name: CR-Int-15-partialfrac-10
questiontext:
Find
\[ \int {{CT:0}} d{{CT:1}} \]
by expressing the integrand in partial fractions.

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]]
generalfeedback:
Since the degree of the numerator is greater than the degree of the denominator we need to use long division the get a simpler form to express \[{{CT:0}}.\] <hint>alg_partial_fractions</hint>

Using long division we get that \[{{CT:0}} = {{CT:2}} + {{CT:3}}\]

Now,

\[{{CT:2}} = {{CT:4}}{{CT:5}} + {{CT:6}}{{CT:7}}\]

So, multiplying by {{CT:8}} both sides we get

\[\begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle
 {{CT:9}} &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:10}} + {{CT:11}} \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:12}}
 \end{array}\]

So, equating cefficients in {{CT:13}} we get that a system of equations that can be solved to get \(A = {{CT:14}}\) and \(B = {{CT:15}}\)

Hence, \[{{CT:0}} = {{CT:16}}\]

So,

\[\begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle
 \int {{CT:0}} d{{CT:1}} &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  \int {{CT:16}} d{{CT:1}} \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:17}} \int {{CT:5}} d{{CT:1}} + {{CT:14}} \int {{CT:7}} d{{CT:1}} + \int ({{CT:3}}) d{{CT:1}} \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:18}} + {{CT:19}} + {{CT:20}}+c \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:21}}+c
 \end{array}\]
